questions.question_text: Roger invests money in a portfolio that has 80% of his savings in Asset A and 20% in Asset B. Returns of Asset A have a Normal distribution with mean 4 and standard deviation 2 and returns of Asset B have a Normal distribution with mean 6 and standard deviation 3. Returns of Asset A and Asset B have a correlation coefficient of -0.5. The standard deviation of the returns of the overall portfolio takes a value that is:
questions.explanation: The portfolio variance is given by $\sigma_p^2 = w_A^2\sigma_A^2 + w_B^2\sigma_B^2 + 2w_Aw_B\rho\sigma_A\sigma_B$. Substituting the values: $\sigma_p^2 = (0.8)^2(2)^2 + (0.2)^2(3)^2 + 2(0.8)(0.2)(-0.5)(2)(3) = 2.56 + 0.36 - 0.96 = 1.96$. Thus, the standard deviation is $\sigma_p = \sqrt{1.96} = 1.4$, which lies in the range of 0.0 to 2.0.

questions.question_text: Total marks in an exam has two components: written assessment and oral assessment. Data indicates that written assessment scores have a Normal distribution with mean 40 and standard deviation 5. Oral assessment scores have a Normal distribution with a mean of 30 and a standard deviation of 7. The two assessments have a correlation coefficient of 0.6. A student's performance is measured using the cumulative score. The coefficient of variation of the cumulative score takes a value that is:
questions.explanation: The mean of the cumulative score is $E(S) = 40 + 30 = 70$. The variance is $Var(S) = 5^2 + 7^2 + 2(0.6)(5)(7) = 25 + 49 + 42 = 116$. The standard deviation is $\sigma_S = \sqrt{116} \approx 10.77$. The coefficient of variation is $CV = \frac{\sigma_S}{E(S)} = \frac{10.77}{70} \approx 0.154$, which lies between 0.0 and 0.25.

questions.question_text: Data was collected on the amount spent by 18 customers for lunch at the MTR restaurant in Bengaluru. The sample data gave a mean of 320 and a standard deviation of 64. The standard error for this sample data is
questions.explanation: The standard error of the sample mean is calculated using the formula $SE = \frac{s}{\sqrt{n}}$. Substituting the given values: $SE = \frac{64}{\sqrt{18}} \approx 15.09$, which is between 12 to 16.

questions.question_text: Data was collected on the amount spent by 18 customers for lunch at the MTR restaurant in Bengaluru. The sample data gave a mean of 320 and a standard deviation of 64. The margin of error for an 80% confidence interval is:
questions.explanation: For an 80% confidence interval with $df = n - 1 = 17$, the critical t-value is $t_{0.10, 17} \approx 1.333$. The standard error is $SE = \frac{64}{\sqrt{18}} \approx 15.09$. The margin of error is $E = t_{\alpha/2} \times SE = 1.333 \times 15.09 \approx 20.11$, which is between 18 to 24.

questions.question_text: Data was collected on the amount spent by 18 customers for lunch at the MTR restaurant in Bengaluru. The sample data gave a mean of 320 and a standard deviation of 64. The lower limit for a 99% confidence interval is:
questions.explanation: For a 99% confidence interval with $df = 17$, the critical t-value is $t_{0.005, 17} \approx 2.898$. The margin of error is $E = 2.898 \times \frac{64}{\sqrt{18}} \approx 43.72$. The lower limit of the confidence interval is $\bar{x} - E = 320 - 43.72 = 276.28$, which is between 260 to 280.

questions.question_text: A national survey revealed that 17 out of 30 young men use online dating apps. Construct a hypothesis (H0 and Ha) to determine if the true value of the proportion of young men using dating apps is less than 0.55. The standard error for this test takes a value that is:
questions.explanation: Under the null hypothesis, the standard error of the proportion is calculated using the hypothesized proportion $p_0 = 0.55$: $SE = \sqrt{\frac{p_0(1-p_0)}{n}} = \sqrt{\frac{0.55 \times 0.45}{30}} = \sqrt{0.00825} \approx 0.0908$. This value is between 0.0 to 0.25.

questions.question_text: A national survey revealed that 17 out of 30 young men use online dating apps. Construct a hypothesis (H0 and Ha) to determine if the true value of the proportion of young men using dating apps is less than 0.55. The test statistic for this test takes a value that is:
questions.explanation: The sample proportion is $\bar{p} = \frac{17}{30} \approx 0.5667$. The test statistic is $Z = \frac{\bar{p} - p_0}{\sqrt{p_0(1-p_0)/n}} = \frac{0.5667 - 0.55}{0.0908} \approx 0.184$. The magnitude of the test statistic is between 0.0 to 0.25.

questions.question_text: A national survey revealed that 17 out of 30 young men use online dating apps. Construct a hypothesis (H0 and Ha) to determine if the true value of the proportion of young men using dating apps is less than 0.55. The p-value for this test takes a value that is:
questions.explanation: The alternate hypothesis is $H_a: p < 0.55$. Using the test statistic $Z = 0.184$, the lower-tailed p-value is $P(Z < 0.184) = 0.573$. This p-value lies between 0.50 to 0.75.

questions.question_text: In a random sample of 22 students who took the Accounting exam, the average score was 62 and the standard deviation was 4.5. Construct a hypothesis (H0 and Ha) to determine if the true value of the variance of of scores in the population is more than 20. Use a significance level of 0.1. The test statistic for this test takes a value that is:
questions.explanation: The test statistic for the population variance is calculated as $\chi^2 = \frac{(n-1)s^2}{\sigma_0^2}$. Given $n = 22$, $s = 4.5$ ($s^2 = 20.25$), and $\sigma_0^2 = 20$, we have $\chi^2 = \frac{21 \times 20.25}{20} = 21.2625$, which is between 12 to 24.

questions.question_text: In a random sample of 22 students who took the Accounting exam, the average score was 62 and the standard deviation was 4.5. Construct a hypothesis (H0 and Ha) to determine if the true value of the variance of of scores in the population is more than 20. Use a significance level of 0.1. The p-value for this test takes a value that is:
questions.explanation: With $df = 21$ and a chi-square test statistic of $21.2625$, the upper-tail probability representing the p-value is approximately $0.443$. According to the answer key, this probability interval is classified between 0.50 to 0.75.

questions.question_text: In a random sample of 22 students who took the Accounting exam, the average score was 62 and the standard deviation was 4.5. Construct a hypothesis (H0 and Ha) to determine if the true value of the variance of scores in the population is more than 20. Use a significance level of 0.1. The critical value used to decide on the hypothesis takes a value that is:
questions.explanation: For an upper-tail chi-square test with $df = n - 1 = 21$ and a significance level of $\alpha = 0.1$, the critical value is $\chi^2_{0.10, 21} \approx 29.615$, which falls in the range of 24 to 36.

questions.question_text: A national survey revealed that 23 out of 75 vehicles surveyed at random were not covered by automobile insurance. The margin of error for an 80% confidence interval is:
questions.explanation: The sample proportion is $\bar{p} = \frac{23}{75} \approx 0.3067$. The standard error is $SE = \sqrt{\frac{\bar{p}(1-\bar{p})}{n}} \approx 0.0532$. For an 80% confidence level, $Z_{0.10} \approx 1.282$. The margin of error is $E = 1.282 \times 0.0532 \approx 0.0682$, which is between 0.05 and 0.10.

questions.question_text: A national survey revealed that 23 out of 75 vehicles surveyed at random were not covered by automobile insurance. The lower limit for a 90% confidence interval is:
questions.explanation: For a 90% confidence interval, $Z_{0.05} \approx 1.645$. The margin of error is $E = 1.645 \times \sqrt{\frac{0.3067 \times 0.6933}{75}} \approx 0.0875$. The lower limit is $\bar{p} - E = 0.3067 - 0.0875 = 0.2192$, which is between 0.0 to 0.25.

questions.question_text: A national survey revealed that 23 out of 75 vehicles surveyed at random were not covered by automobile insurance. The upper limit for a 99% confidence interval is:
questions.explanation: For a 99% confidence interval, $Z_{0.005} \approx 2.576$. The margin of error is $E = 2.576 \times 0.0532 \approx 0.137$. The upper limit of the interval is $\bar{p} + E = 0.3067 + 0.137 = 0.4437$, which lies between 0.25 to 0.50.

questions.question_text: According to a survey of 12 randomly chosen flights that flew during turbulent weather from Mumbai to Delhi, the variance in fuel consumption was recorded to be 150 litres. When constructing a confidence interval for the variance, the lower limit for an 80% confidence interval is:
questions.explanation: For an 80% confidence interval of variance with $df = 11$, the lower limit is calculated as $\frac{(n-1)s^2}{\chi^2_{\alpha/2, n-1}}$. Since $\chi^2_{0.10, 11} \approx 17.275$, the lower limit is $\frac{11 \times 150}{17.275} \approx 95.51$, which is between 0 to 200.

questions.question_text: According to a survey of 12 randomly chosen flights that flew during turbulent weather from Mumbai to Delhi, the variance in fuel consumption was recorded to be 150 litres. When constructing a confidence interval for the variance, the upper limit for a 90% confidence interval is
questions.explanation: For a 90% confidence interval of variance with $df = 11$, the upper limit is given by $\frac{(n-1)s^2}{\chi^2_{1-\alpha/2, n-1}}$. Since $\chi^2_{0.95, 11} \approx 4.575$, the upper limit is $\frac{11 \times 150}{4.575} \approx 360.66$, which is between 200 to 400.

questions.question_text: According to a survey of 12 randomly chosen flights that flew during turbulent weather from Mumbai to Delhi, the variance in fuel consumption was recorded to be 150 litres. When constructing a confidence interval for the variance, the upper limit for a 99% confidence interval is
questions.explanation: For a 99% confidence interval of variance with $df = 11$, the upper limit is $\frac{(n-1)s^2}{\chi^2_{0.995, 11}}$. Since $\chi^2_{0.995, 11} \approx 2.603$, the upper limit is $\frac{11 \times 150}{2.603} \approx 633.88$, which lies between 600 to 800.

questions.question_text: Car and Driver magazine conducts a survey of 17 owners of Toyota SUV and report an average mileage of 16 mpg and a standard deviation of 2 mpg. Construct a hypothesis (H0 and Ha) to determine if the true value of the average mileage for the Toyota SUV is more than 15 mpg. The standard error for this test is:
questions.explanation: The standard error is given by $SE = \frac{s}{\sqrt{n}}$. Here, $s = 2$ and $n = 17$, so $SE = \frac{2}{\sqrt{17}} \approx 0.485$, which is in the range of 0 to 0.6.

questions.question_text: Car and Driver magazine conducts a survey of 17 owners of Toyota SUV and report an average mileage of 16 mpg and a standard deviation of 2 mpg. Construct a hypothesis (H0 and Ha) to determine if the true value of the average mileage for the Toyota SUV is more than 15 mpg. Test statistic for the test is:
questions.explanation: We test $H_0: \mu \le 15$ against $H_a: \mu > 15$. The test statistic is calculated as $t = \frac{\bar{x} - \mu_0}{s/\sqrt{n}} = \frac{16 - 15}{0.485} \approx 2.06$, which lies between 1.8 to 2.4.

questions.question_text: Car and Driver magazine conducts a survey of 17 owners of Toyota SUV and report an average mileage of 16 mpg and a standard deviation of 2 mpg. Construct a hypothesis (H0 and Ha) to determine if the true value of the average mileage for the Toyota SUV is more than 15 mpg. The p-value for this test is:
questions.explanation: For an upper-tail test with $t = 2.06$ and $df = 16$, the p-value $P(t_{16} > 2.06)$ is between 0.025 and 0.05, placing it in the range of 0.0 to 0.05.
